sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the request] Ukraine is convening an emergency UN Security Council meeting over Russian strikes on Dnipro, Chernihiv and Kremenchuk; Melnyk signed a letter to the Council president (Greece) requesting an extraordinary meeting. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Melnyk's wording] 'Following Russia's latest barbaric atrocities against Ukrainian civilians in Dnipro, Chernihiv & Kremenchuk, where Russian missiles deliberately slaughtered 20 Ukrainians & wounded dozens more, we are convening an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council. Kick Russia out.' [TOLL DISCREPANCY -- DO NOT SETTLE] Melnyk's figure is 20 killed in the three cities; Kyiv Post reports at least 25 dead and 110 wounded nationwide; Kyiv Independent cites local authorities for at least 27 killed and 128 injured across Ukraine over the past day. The figures differ by scope (three cities vs nationwide vs past-day) and are NOT reconciled in the retrieved reporting. [VERIFIED FACT] No meeting date was specified in the retrieved reporting (Interfax: Melnyk 'did not specify the date'). Oct 30 was declared a day of mourning for Dnipro, Chernihiv and Poltava region.
sections.what_verified: Kyiv Independent (T2) + Ukrinform (T2, STATE-UA) = 2 distinct publisher families carrying Melnyk's statement and the MFA position. Kyiv Post, United24, RBC-Ukraine, LB.ua relays carry no declared tier in the registry and are not counted.
sections.what_disputed: Russia, as a P5 member, can veto substantive Council resolutions -- the structural counterpoint to the 'kick Russia out' demand; no Russian response to the meeting request retrieved. Moscow's standing line (denies targeting civilians; rail/infrastructure strikes aim at military movement) is the counter-claim for the underlying strikes, not a response to the UNSC request. Russia's UN envoy position on the request itself is unretrieved.
sections.why_matters: Ukraine takes Dnipro, Chernihiv and Kremenchuk to the Security Council -- and demands the country that bombed them be kicked out of the room that can veto it.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Oct 30 evening, absent from Oct 30/31 scans) -- Ukraine convenes emergency UN Security Council meeting over Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kremenchuk strikes; Melnyk: 'Kick Russia out'

totw_analysis: Our read: Ukraine takes Dnipro, Chernihiv and Kremenchuk to the Security Council -- and demands the country that bombed them be kicked out of the room that can veto it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: An emergency Council meeting where the accused holds a veto -- accountability theatre, or the only stage that forces the strikes onto the record?
